Content:
Suppose we want to calculate the sum
[MATH: S_N = \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{5} 3 (4)^{n-1}.]

Content:
Notice that this series is in the form [MATH: \displaystyle{\sum_{n=1}^N a_1 r^{n-1}},] which represents a geometric series.

Content:
To determine the sum, we can use the formula for the sum [MATH: S_N] of a geometric series:
[MATH: S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}]

Content:
In this case, [MATH: a_1 = 3,] [MATH: r = 4,] and [MATH: N = 5.] If we substitute these values into the formula for [MATH: S_N,] we obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(n = 1)^(5)3(4)^{n − 1}|= 3 ⋅ ((1 − 4^{5})/(1 − 4)); = 3 ⋅ ((− 1023)/(− 3)); = 1023]

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum [MATH: S_N] of a geometric series: [MATH: S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}]

In this case, [MATH: a_1 = 3,] [MATH: r = 2,] and [MATH: N = 8.] If we substitute these values into the formula for [MATH: S_N,] we obtain the following:

[MATH: ∑_(n = 1)^(8)3(2)^{n − 1}|= 3 ⋅ ((1 − 2^{8})/(1 − 2)); = 3 ⋅ ((− 255)/(− 1)); = 765]

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum [MATH: S_N] of a geometric series: [MATH: S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}]

In this case, [MATH: a_1 =8,] [MATH: r = \dfrac{1}{2},] and [MATH: N = 5.] If we substitute these values into the above formula, we obtain the following:

[MATH: ∑_(n = 1)^(5)(8)/(2^{n − 1})|= 8 ⋅ ([1 − ((1)/(2))^{5}])/((1 − (1)/(2))); = 8 ⋅ (((31)/(32)))/(((1)/(2))); = 8 ⋅ (31)/(16); = (31)/(2)]
